1#main: They bury gentile dead and console their mourners because of ways of peace.
2#main: One should not walk in the cemetery or within four amot of the dead with tefillin on his head because of 'one who mocks the poor'; and if they are covered — permitted.
3#main: One should not walk in the cemetery or within four amot of the dead or of a grave with a Sefer Torah in his arm and read in it or pray; and the same for by heart — forbidden to read unless for the honor of the dead as explained (and see below siman 344 seif 16).
4#main: It is permitted to enter the cemetery or within four amot of the dead or grave while wearing tzitzit, provided it not drag on the grave; but if it drags — forbidden because of 'one who mocks the poor.' In what case? In their days when they attached tzitzit to garments they wore for themselves; but nowadays when we wear it only for the mitzvah — forbidden even if not dragging {Rama: And these matters when the tzitzit are exposed; but if covered — permitted.}
5#main: Some practice tying the two tzitzit on the two corners together when entering the cemetery — and this did not help their enactment (and see in Orach Chaim siman 23).
6#main: Once he distanced four amot he reads and prays, even if he sees the grave or cemetery; and if there is a partition there — permitted beyond the partition even adjacent within four amot of the grave.
